reviews.title: Misleading “Monthly VIP” Experience
reviews.text:
Today I purchased the “Monthly VIP” experience for $32. I expected a time based access consistent with the term “monthly.” Instead, the subscription provides only a limited number of coins, which allowed me to watch 1, almost 2, dramas before depletion. 
In practice this was comparable to renting a movie for $16 each. The experience is further limited by the inability to fast forward or skip episodes. This reduced my flexibility and I felt the value of my purchase. 
The term “monthly” is misleading as it’s not based on duration but on a very restricted consumption limit. 
This should have been distinct at the time of purchase instead I had to find out at the climax of a drama that I ran out of coins and required more coins on the first day of the “subscription.”
This experience doesn’t align with a reasonable customer experience.
Based on this I would caution potential subscribers or buyers to read the fine print.

Other drama apps  I’ve used don’t do this, usually their episodes cost the same price but Kalos doesn’t practice this. I shouldn’t have to pay almost a 100 dollars to watch 31 episodes on one drama.
